summary: The change meets the user's decisions. The Gemini episode summary runs on its own daemon worker (ERIS-LivingUserEpisode). The turn buffer lock is held only to snapshot and to trim by (id, timestamp) key. The model call runs outside every lock, with a 60 s adapter timeout plus a 65 s hard deadline, single flight, exponential backoff capped at 600 s, and deferral while a user turn is active. A failed or timed-out call keeps the turns and writes no episode; the heuristic fallback is used only when there is no adapter or the buffer holds 40 or more rows. The episode is persisted before the buffer is trimmed. A hard-forget racing with an in-flight call is covered by episode_store._blocked_evidence. OCR is off by default behind ERIS_SCREEN_OCR_ENABLED: no RapidOCR/pytesseract import, no pip self-heal, no force_ocr from chat, and an explicit screen reference goes to vision on the same turn. I found no blocker or major issue. Minor gaps remain: backoff also blocks the buffer-pressure fallback, the worker is not cancelled by maintenance clear, shutdown does not stop the worker, and the 6th failing test is not listed in the 5 known failures.

findings.issue: The backoff gate (`time.monotonic() < self._cons_next_at`) in _consolidation_loop also blocks the buffer-pressure heuristic fallback. During a long Gemini outage with active chat (backoff reaches 240-600 s), the buffer can grow past 48 rows before the next run. `record_conversation_turn` then silently drops the oldest rows with `[-48:]` and no episode is written. Lower severity because the 48-row cap and the fallback at 40 rows are the pre-existing design.
findings.fix: In the worker loop, bypass `_cons_next_at` when `len(self._turn_buffer) >= episode_fallback_rows`. The next run is then `pressure` and writes the heuristic episode before the cap drops rows. Add a test for it.

findings.issue: The 'forget user model' clear (`_clear_runtime_user_context`) does not cancel or fence the consolidation worker. An in-flight call (up to 60 s) can still call `episode_store.add` after the files are wiped and recreate living_user_episodes.json. Hard forget() is protected by `_blocked_evidence`, but this wipe is not. The race existed before in a different form (the old flush also ran after the wipe). Also pre-existing: this function clears `episode_store._episodes`, which does not exist (the store uses `_items`). The AttributeError is caught, so the turn-buffer clear below it never runs.
findings.fix: Optional, separate task. Add a generation counter on the service that clear/hard-forget bump, and have `_consolidate_once` discard the result and skip the trim if it changed during the call. Fix the `_episodes` attribute name separately.

findings.issue: `stop_consolidation()` has no caller outside tests. On shutdown the worker is a daemon thread blocked on `Event.wait(None)` and is not stopped explicitly. An in-flight call is abandoned at process exit.
findings.fix: Call `living_user.stop_consolidation()` from the owner's shutdown path if it already stops other background services; otherwise document that daemon exit is intended.

findings.issue: The report says `test_companion_memory_authority_consolidation.py::test_living_user_competence_claim_is_context_only_not_teaching_authority` was 'not confirmed against baseline HEAD'. I ran it on a `git archive HEAD` copy and it fails there too, with the same symptom as the two v39 failures (compile_context returns no profile item). So 6 failures are pre-existing, not 5, and context.json lists only 5. It is not a regression.
findings.fix: Update report.md and context.json to list it as a confirmed pre-existing failure.

findings.issue: No test covers a retry after backoff succeeding, the backoff growth (60, 120, ... capped at 600 s), or the deferred path through the real `GLOBAL_INFERENCE_BROKER` gate (the tests override `_user_turn_active`). These paths are untested; with a base delay of at least 60 s, retry timing cannot be tested without an injectable clock. The tests that exist use event synchronisation and wait_until with 6-8 s ceilings, and I saw no timing flakiness.
findings.fix: Optional: make `_cons_next_at` testable (monkeypatch `time.monotonic` or set `episode_retry_sec` small) and add a fail-then-succeed test.
